preconditions.description: The number of words N is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(lengths) == N and all(1 <= l <= 1000 for l in lengths)
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly N integers representing word lengths, each between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' if not exists_valid_set else (stdout.splitlines()[0] == 'YES' and len(stdout.splitlines()) == N + 1 and all(w in '01' for w in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and all(len(w) == lengths[i] for i, w in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1:])) and all(not any(w2.startswith(w1) for w1 in stdout.splitlines()[1:] if w1 != w2) for w2 in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: If no valid set of words exists, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by N binary strings matching the input lengths in order, such that no string is a prefix of another.
A valid set exists if and only if the sum of 2^(-length) for all lengths is at most 1 (Kraft's inequality for binary prefix codes).
